name: ND at-large
label: Safe R

key_factors: North Dakota's R+18 partisan lean anchors the race firmly Republican
Fedorchak holds a roughly six-to-one fundraising edge ($2.1M vs. $341K raised) and $1M+ cash on hand
Prediction markets give Hammer about a two percent win probability
No public polling shows any sign of competitiveness
model.rationale: North Dakota's eighteen-point Republican lean, Fedorchak's incumbency and dominant fundraising advantage, and prediction markets pricing a Democratic upset at roughly two percent all point to an easy Republican hold, with no polling evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: A strong national Democratic midterm wave or a late infusion of outside spending for Hammer could narrow the margin, though no such spending is currently in evidence.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North Dakota's at-large House seat sits in strongly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of roughly eighteen points toward the GOP. Republican Julie Fedorchak, first elected in 2024, is running for re-election and enters with a large financial edge, having raised about $2.1 million and holding more than $1 million on hand. Democrat Trygve Hammer, her general-election opponent again this cycle, has raised roughly $341,000 and trails badly in cash on hand. Two independent candidates are also on the ballot but show no fundraising activity.

No public polls of the race are available, and prediction markets give Democrats only about a two percent chance of an upset. The structural fundamentals—district lean, incumbency, and the money gap—all point the same direction. Barring an unforeseen development, this seat is expected to remain comfortably in Republican hands.
